# `property-became-optional`

Property became optional

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-became-optional` (both directions), `property-became-optional-in-request`, `property-became-optional-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A required property is now optional.

## Why this default

In requests: clients that send it keep working. In responses: clients may assume it is always present and fail when it is missing.

## Example

From test case [`property-became-optional`](../../test/cases/property-became-optional/): A required response property became optional.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-       required:
-       - name
```

Findings:

- `property-became-optional-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  property-became-optional: error
```

## How to fix

In responses, keep returning the property.
